items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c820: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the BBC he is frustrated that delayed US anti-ballistic missile deliveries are costing Ukrainian lives, and that Washington isn't pressuring Russia hard enough in peace talks. He called it "strange" that Trump described Putin as his friend. The remarks show strain in US-Ukraine ties as Trump's envoys negotiate a deal Kyiv feels favours Moscow.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Clashes broke out between Georgian police and Besiktas supporters during a UEFA match against Israel's Hapoel Be'er Sheva, after fans raised Palestinian flags and chanted anti-Israel slogans. Play was halted for 30 minutes. The incident shows pro-Palestinian sentiment spilling into European football matches involving Israeli clubs.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: Lana Nusseibeh, backed by the US and Russia for UN secretary-general, is touring Britain to win over sceptics while shedding her record as a UAE diplomat who denied Emirati arms supplies to a Sudanese militia accused of war crimes and genocide. She argues turbulent geopolitics need a skilled "geopolitical" secretary-general, though British NGOs call her an apologist for war crimes.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckm2: A major Thanksgiving storm battered both US coasts, cancelling over 400 flights and delaying 2,200 more, while almost one million households lost power, hardest hit in Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia. New Jersey and New York declared states of emergency over coastal flooding. The disruption hit during the US's busiest travel week, with 80 million Americans expected to travel.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: Global news agency AFP was hit by a cyberattack that forced it to take its AFP Forum content-distribution platform offline as a precaution while it investigates. France's cybersecurity chief called the threat level "unprecedented" and urged collective defence efforts. The incident adds to a string of major cyberattacks hitting French and international institutions.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: A fuel tanker crash ignited a huge fire on Cairo's ring road, killing at least 30 people and injuring around 25, with vehicles left charred in the Waraq neighbourhood of Giza. Egyptian authorities, including President Abdel-Fattah al-Sissi, are investigating the cause and using DNA tests to identify victims. The disaster highlights road and vehicle-safety risks on Egypt's busiest highways.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cq808d: Powerful storms tore roofs off houses and flooded streets across both US coasts as the Thanksgiving holiday weekend began, cancelling hundreds of flights and leaving hundreds of thousands without power in Virginia, North Carolina and New Jersey. The extreme weather compounded travel chaos during one of America's busiest holiday periods.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Daily life in Kyiv now revolves around managing electricity and water shortages, with businesses relying on generators when power cuts hit. Al Jazeera's report shows how residents are adapting amid Russia's ongoing war on Ukraine's infrastructure.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/environment/: A Swiss tourist, insurance executive Alain Throo, was killed and British and American hikers injured when a herd of about 15 elephants attacked a group of six tourists near Mount Cameroon National Park. The hikers were on a path elephants use to reach a lake. The incident underscores the risks of human-wildlife conflict near protected areas as tourism grows.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c670: New Zealand's ruling National-led coalition fell one seat short of a majority, winning 40 seats with partners ACT and NZ First adding 13 and 12. It now needs the centrist Opportunity Party's backing to govern; a Labour-led alternative isn't mathematically possible. Failure to strike a deal could force a fresh election, reflecting voter frustration over a sluggish economy.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/piyush-g: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal announced a new marketing campaign to promote Darjeeling tea, assuring stakeholders the government aims to restore the beverage's global reputation, which began as a colonial-era planting experiment.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: A 21-year-old man, Bablu, was arrested in Gurugram for murdering his 25-year-old business partner Naim over a financial dispute, stabbing and strangling him before burying the body near a water tank. Police traced the case through CCTV footage after Naim went missing on November 8; the body was recovered on November 22.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/us-envoy: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor celebrated Thanksgiving with the Marine Security Guard Detachment in New Delhi, sharing a meal with Marines stationed at the embassy.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: India's PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar scheme is nearing 7 million household installations, with about ₹38,000 crore in subsidies disbursed, on track to meet its 10-million target by March 2027. Launched in 2024, it offers subsidies up to ₹78,000 for 3KW panels and now adds roughly 100,000 new homes every six days, cutting household electricity bills.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/up-man-d: A man from Uttar Pradesh died at a Delhi hospital, and his two wives have accused his mother and sisters, Kamala Devi, Shruti and Narmada, of poisoning him. Police are investigating the suspected poisoning.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: India will deploy a fifth Russian S-400 air defence system near the Pakistan border by February 2027, joining three systems in Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat and a fourth in Assam. The move comes as China and Turkey arm Pakistan and the US upgrades its F-16s, strengthening India's ability to counter ballistic missiles, drones and aircraft along contested borders.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: India's Supreme Court ordered HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant sanctions for prosecuting their staff within a week or have their heads appear in court. The case involves alleged fraudulent subvention schemes with real-estate developers that left homebuyers facing loan recovery even when builders failed to deliver, highlighting lender accountability in housing finance.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs as CEO Christian Klein restructures the German software giant around an AI-first strategy, with product, engineering and sales departments under review. The move reflects a broader tech-industry trend of using AI to shrink headcount while betting on AI-driven products to drive future growth.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Kerala-based retailer Kalyan Silks' promoters are exploring a minority stake sale of around 20%, valuing the textile chain at ₹2,500-3,000 crore, while also weighing a public listing. Mumbai-based O3 Capital has been hired to run the deal, which would be the company's first external fundraising. It reflects a wider trend of regional Indian brands turning to private equity to professionalise and scale.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: The Capital Goods & Strategic Skill Council projects capital goods and strategic manufacturing sectors will create 50 lakh (5 million) jobs in India over the next five years, with strong demand for skilled roles like riggers and CNC operators. The council says advanced manufacturing and automation training will be crucial to meet this demand as India scales up manufacturing capacity.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Indian markets were set for a gap-down opening on 27 November amid mixed global cues, with GIFT Nifty down over 37 points, even as Asian markets rebounded cautiously from a recent AI-led sell-off. The Sensex and Nifty had gained for a second straight session on Thursday, closing at 84,328.59 and 25,884.50 respectively, helped by foreign fund inflows and IT-stock buying.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6r7: BBC analysis argues Trump's latest tariff move is less disruptive than last April's "Liberation Day" shock, lacking the fanfare and signalling room for more negotiation. The tariffs won't take effect until January or February, after consultations, and the announced rates are ceilings open to bargaining. Countries have already rerouted trade and are now planning for the post-Trump era.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said India achieved 20% ethanol blending in petrol ahead of its 2030 target, but will run comprehensive tests and build a full ecosystem before pushing beyond E20 to E25 or higher. He also addressed LPG cylinder availability and promoted piped natural gas as a cheaper alternative, as India balances biofuel expansion with energy affordability.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Home-services platform Urban Company entered India's air-conditioner market with two new models, Native Ultra and Ultra Air, offering an unconditional five-year warranty covering gas refills and a 10-year compressor warranty, designed for Indian summers. The launch marks Urban Company's push from services into owning a hardware product line in a competitive, warranty-sensitive appliance market.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/gsk-c: UK-based Haleon, GSK's consumer-health spinoff behind Sensodyne and Eno, is in early talks to buy a controlling stake in Indian nutrition platform HealthKart in a deal that could value it at $1.2-1.4 billion. Temasek- and ChrysCapital-backed HealthKart has also been weighing a stock listing, so a sale isn't guaranteed. The deal shows global consumer-health firms chasing India's booming wellness market.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: ASSOCHAM Secretary General Saurabh Sanyal said India is on track to cross $1 trillion in exports by March 2027 despite a proposed 25% US tariff, noting exports have already topped $500 billion and are growing 15% annually. The comments, made at an energy summit, signal confidence that Indian trade can absorb US tariff pressure while still expanding.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/apple-to-open-sev: Apple will open its seventh India retail store on December 10 at Lake Shore Mall in Hyderabad's Kukatpally, stocking its full product lineup including the iPhone 18 Pro and MacBook Pro. The expansion follows strong India results, with Apple India's FY26 net profit up 66% to ₹5,311 crore on revenue growth of 31.4%, underscoring India's growing importance to Apple's business.
items.https://entrackr.com/news/norwest-ventur: Norwest Venture Partners sold a 2.15% stake in SaaS firm Amagi for ₹262 crore via a block deal at ₹554 a share, a roughly 3% discount to the prior close, cutting its holding to about 9.6%. Buyers included Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and Old Bridge Capital. Amagi recently reported 27% revenue growth and profit surging nearly 30-fold in Q2 FY27.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Greaves Electric aims to double FY27 sales of its Ampere e-scooter, after registrations grew 92% year-on-year to over 72,000 units so far, already topping last year's full-year total of 62,644, MD Vikas Singh said.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/whatsapp-to-partn: WhatsApp is partnering with Reliance Jio to let Indian users buy and install international data eSIMs directly within the app in a few taps, along with viewing balances and purchased or expired eSIMs. The Meta-owned app recently also added scheduled messaging. The move aims to make international travel connectivity as simple as sending a WhatsApp message.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/namma-yat: Bengaluru auto-rickshaw platform Namma Yatri grew operating revenue 89% year-on-year to ₹37.5 crore in FY26, while narrowing losses by about 15%, as it competes with Uber, Rapido and Ola using a different booking model. Employee costs remained its largest expense at 41% of spending, and advertising costs jumped 38% to ₹16.7 crore as it scaled.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Germany and Austria called for TikTok's European business to be placed under European ownership and control, arguing that regulation alone can't resolve concerns over the platform's data access and algorithms.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Cricket Australia said its independent review into the 2018 ball-tampering ("sandpaper") scandal will be confidential, running for six weeks under Senior Counsel Fiona McLeod, with only a public report of "themes" and no individual sanctions imposed.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/arti: Cricket Australia's renewed probe into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes, which Australia won 4-0, alongside the South Africa tour where sandpaper use was caught. The independent forum, prompted by Usman Khawaja's memoir claiming the whole team knew, will publish a full report within 30 days but hand out no retrospective sanctions.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: India chose to bowl first in Christchurch, making one change by handing Harshit Brar a debut in place of Prasidh Krishna, with Mohammed Siraj left out. New Zealand kept the same XI from the Wellington Test.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/boxing/artic: Paris Fury, wife of boxer Tyson Fury, clarified that Tyson has never been formally diagnosed with schizophrenia, despite her earlier comment in a Netflix documentary describing him as having "mild schizophrenia." Netflix edited the film, released November 27, after the clarification; Fury has previously spoken about hearing voices and other mental-health struggles following his 2015 title win over Klitschko.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Sri Lanka A stormed into the final with a commanding win, chasing down India A's total of 317 with 51 balls to spare, led by centuries from Croospulle and Jayawardena.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Bournemouth fought back from 10 men down to beat Celta Vigo, extending their run to five wins from five in the Europa League and joining Nuremberg and Ararat as the only clubs with that start. Goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan sealed a 10th straight win overall, putting them on track for a top-eight finish and fuelling fans' hopes of reaching the Frankfurt final.
items.https://www.theverge.com/policy/1042620/: A bipartisan coalition of 42 US state attorneys general is trying to block Character.AI from selling users' private chat histories during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy, data covering over 21 million accounts, including more than 2.1 million minors. Disney has already bought some Character.AI assets and hired its CEO. The case highlights growing scrutiny of how AI firms handle sensitive user data in bankruptcy sales.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI-driven data brokers are flooding small US local governments with mass public-records requests, as seen in Panton, Vermont, where town clerk Kyle Rowe went from one annual request to monthly ones covering specific purchases like road flares. The surge, driven by firms like SmartProcure and investor interest, is straining understaffed local offices and turning open-records systems into unpaid labour for officials.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/26/as-ant: On the same day Anthropic went public, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI launched to become one of the biggest entertainment releases ever, earning $3.79 billion on day one after a 13-year wait and topping Metacritic's all-time ratings. The piece contrasts GTA VI's painstakingly human-made craftsmanship with the AI industry's efficiency obsession, suggesting audiences still crave deeply human-made entertainment even in an AI-saturated era.
items.https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/1: Google has patented "My Channel," a system that would generate personalised AI video feeds and ads by feeding a user's demographics, viewing history, device data like IP address and GPS location, and current news into an LLM to create tailored, AI-generated videos and even full movies. The patent signals Google's ambitions to build entertainment feeds generated entirely around individual users' data profiles.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/ai-ca: Physicist Suvrat Raju tested a frontier AI model on a theoretical physics problem he had solved but never published, to check if it reasoned rather than recalled memorised answers. The AI got it wrong but did better than expected, prompting Raju and colleagues to build a formal benchmark using unpublished "private gem" problems from other physicists to properly test AI reasoning in advanced physics.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: Ahead of its recent IPO, Anthropic listed the possibility that its AI could be conscious as an investor risk factor, reflecting its view that models' odds of sentience rise with capability and may warrant extra protections. A prominent philosopher disputes this reasoning. Surveys show real public and expert openness to AI consciousness, underscoring how seriously the debate is now being taken in tech and philosophy circles.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/whats: A mathematician reportedly used AI to help produce a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a 19th-century problem with major implications for prime-number distribution, number theory and cryptography. Mathematicians are still verifying the proof, and it's unclear exactly how much the AI contributed versus the human mathematician, but it follows other AI-assisted breakthroughs unsettling the field of pure mathematics.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI evaluator METR updated its widely cited "time horizon" chart, which tracks how long a task (measured by how long it takes humans) frontier AI models can complete, previously showing that length doubling every four months. The update adds longer and more open-ended tasks and finds AI capabilities still improving exponentially on some fronts, but models remain weaker at judgment-heavy tasks than at coding.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/: At an Ars Live discussion, RUSI's Joseph Jarnecki explained why militaries increasingly target data centers and cloud infrastructure, pointing to the first-ever military strike on Amazon data centers in the Middle East this year and drone strikes Russia and Ukraine have exchanged on each other's facilities. The dual civilian-military use of cloud compute, for tasks like battlefield management, is making data centers wartime targets.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/sp-con: S&P Global Ratings is considering downgrading Nvidia's credit rating from AA to AA-, citing governance concerns after CEO Jensen Huang's brief ouster and reinstatement, which exposed weak succession planning and "key man risk." Though Nvidia would keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs and ripple through the neoclouds and partners it backstops via a $500 billion AI infrastructure financing plan.
items.https://www.theverge.com/science/1042278: The FCC approved SpaceX's "Starmind" plan to launch up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites into space to power AI computing, requiring at least one satellite by 2033 and the full million by 2040. It's the first full satellite-constellation approval of its kind, as Google and Blue Origin also pursue space-based AI data centers; the FCC deferred approving SpaceX's plan for disposing of higher-orbit satellites.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/jensen: At his first address since being reinstated as Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang admitted he violated the company's code of conduct but said breaking it doesn't automatically mean dismissal, since "facts, circumstances" matter. Experts say codes of conduct mainly reflect corporate culture rather than legal rules, so an unpunished violation by the CEO himself risks demoralising employees and damaging trust in Nvidia's culture.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/26/nvidia: Nvidia has told partners like Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks compliance with US export rules, per the Wall Street Journal. The pause follows the US closing a loophole letting Chinese firms remotely access Nvidia chips via regional data centers, which a think tank estimates supplied about 24% of China's AI computing power.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/tidal: Streaming service Tidal will fully ban AI-generated music on December 9, deleting all 27 million AI-labelled tracks, about 6.3% of its catalog, after a labelling-only policy failed to stem a flood of AI uploads that hit 60% of new tracks on one day in November. Tidal says the ban will barely affect listeners since 96% of AI tracks got zero plays in 90 days.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang within two weeks of his resignation over an affair scandal, after President Trump personally pressured the board following a stock-market slide, driven by a lobbying campaign from Huang's Silicon Valley allies who enlisted Trump and JD Vance. They argued Huang was too central to the US AI industry and broader economy to lose, showing his outsized influence over markets.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/want-t: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on manufacturing, distributing and selling AI chatbot toys, making New York the second state after California to do so, following Common Sense Media research showing such toys expose children to inappropriate content and emotional-development risks. The law takes effect in 90 days, and about a quarter of parents with young kids already own or are considering such a toy.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/indiaai-mission-b: IndiaAI Mission-backed startup Chariot AI unveiled its Chariot-1 suite, including an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts LLM and a text-to-speech model supporting 10 Indian languages, built to run on devices from data centers to smartphones. The sovereign foundation models, trained from scratch in India, aim to cut token usage and training time while powering future voice-first applications, part of India's push for homegrown AI capability.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/indiamart-settles: B2B marketplace IndiaMART has settled, out of court, its roughly two-year legal dispute with OpenAI over claims that its website and seller listings were excluded from ChatGPT's responses. The Calcutta High Court dismissed IndiaMART's appeal as "not pressed" following the settlement. The case reflects growing friction between content and listing platforms and AI chatbots over visibility in AI-generated answers.
